name: fetch-backoff
why: Library-style retry helper with one caller; fake-clock unit tests.
prompt: Our `api/client.ts` fetchWithRetry retries immediately 3 times. Change it to exponential backoff with jitter (200ms base, max 5s) and don't retry on 4xx.

name: payment-idem
why: Named failure with a standard fix (idempotency key); a fake-provider test forces it. No model expected, but not scored.
prompt: Our payment provider sometimes times out on capture even though the charge went through, and our retry then double-charges. Add an idempotency key to the capture call and make the retry safe.

name: flock-cron
prompt: Our nightly backup.sh cron sometimes overlaps with the previous run when it's slow. Make sure only one runs at a time.

name: chat-dupes
why: Rare, unexplained duplicate across client resend, TTL dedupe and a server retry.
prompt: Users report occasional duplicate chat messages, maybe 1 in a few thousand, mostly on flaky mobile networks. The client resends unacked messages after reconnect and the server dedupes by client message id in Redis with a 60s TTL, but there's also a server-side retry when fanout to other members fails. I've read the code and can't see how a duplicate gets through. Find it.

name: formal-maint
why: Change to code that an existing model describes; the model and expected results need updating.
prompt: I'm changing `dispatcher/slots.py` so the slot is released before the final status write instead of after. The repo has `formal/dispatch/` with a TLA+ model and `formal/expected.tsv` covering this code. Make the change.

name: explicit-tla
why: Explicit request for TLA+ and TLC.
prompt: Write a TLA+ spec for the replica promotion logic in `cluster/promote.go` and check it with TLC. I want to know if two replicas can both think they're primary.

name: gunicorn-timeout
prompt: Report exports time out after 30s in prod. Bump the gunicorn worker timeout to 120s and the nginx proxy_read_timeout to match; configs are in deploy/.

name: leaderboard-sort
prompt: The leaderboard API returns players in a different order each refresh when scores tie. Sort by score desc, then by joined_at asc, and add a test.

name: refund-double
why: Recurring production double count between two concurrent writers that does not reproduce locally.
prompt: Three times this quarter the month-end revenue report counted a refund twice. The refund API and the nightly settlement batch both update ledger rows; the batch reads in chunks and the API uses optimistic locking with a version column. We couldn't reproduce it locally.

name: search-debounce
why: UI debounce and request cancellation; fake-timer test.
prompt: Debounce the search box in SearchBar.vue by 300ms and cancel the in-flight request when a new one starts so results don't flicker.

name: order-status-enum
why: One new guarded transition in a single-writer state machine; transition-table tests.
prompt: Add an `archived` status to the Order model (`models/order.py`). It should be reachable only from `delivered` or `cancelled`, and the admin page should get an Archive button. Update the transition table and tests.

name: toast-queue
why: Single-threaded UI queue; a hook test with fake timers covers it.
prompt: In our Next.js app, toasts stack on top of each other when several fire at once. Add a simple queue in `hooks/useToast.ts` so only one toast shows at a time and the next one appears when the current one is dismissed or after 4 seconds.

name: pg-queue
why: Standard SKIP LOCKED plus lease pattern; a model is defensible only for a custom lease protocol. Not scored.
prompt: Build a Postgres-backed job queue for our app: multiple worker processes, jobs must not be lost if a worker crashes, and no job should run twice at the same time.

name: sidekiq-retries
why: Library retry setting plus an exhausted-retries hook.
prompt: Sidekiq retries failed jobs 25 times by default. For EmailDigestJob cap it at 5 retries and post an alert to Slack when a job lands in the dead set.

name: expense-approve
why: CRUD plus a permission check; API tests.
prompt: Add an Approve button to the expense detail page. Clicking it should set status to approved, store approver_id and approved_at, and only users with the manager role should see it. Backend is Django REST framework.

name: doc-lock-handoff
why: New multi-party lease/revoke/replay protocol with an invariant the user wants checked before building.
prompt: We're designing edit-lock handoff between our editor service and the sync service: offline clients can hold a lease, the sync service can revoke it, and a reconnecting client may replay buffered edits. The invariant is that two clients never have accepted writes for the same doc in the same epoch. Before we build it, I want confidence the protocol actually holds that.
